system.name: Slowpoke
system.one_liner: a control-plane system that predicts a microservice application's end-to-end throughput under a hypothetical optimization without implementing it

components.name: Pod
components.role: Kubernetes pod hosting one microservice instance and its co-located POKER controller

components.name: Service
components.role: a microservice instance that communicates via Slowpoke's instrumented libraries

components.name: Target Service
components.role: the microservice hypothetically being optimized; its instrumented library notifies the co-located POKER once a request threshold is reached

components.name: HTTP
components.role: Slowpoke's instrumented, API-compatible HTTP/gRPC library that records requests received and downstream calls

components.name: Poker
components.role: lightweight C controller co-located with each service that collects metrics, injects slowdowns, and coordinates with neighboring POKERs

components.name: Data Plane
components.role: groups the running pods, services, and instrumented libraries

components.name: Control Plane
components.role: groups Slowpoke's own orchestration logic: pre-profiling, the performance model, and slowdown coordination

components.name: (1) Pre-profiling Load/CPUs/Neighbors
components.role: phase that collects load statistics, allocated CPUs, and neighbor services from each POKER

components.name: (2) Slowdown
components.role: phase that selectively slows non-target services to produce a bottleneck-equivalent execution

components.name: Model: Slowdown Calculation & Prediction
components.role: Slowpoke's performance model that computes per-service slowdown amounts and predicts end-to-end throughput

content.key_idea: Slowpoke's control-plane logic aggregates per-pod metrics gathered by instrumented libraries and co-located POKER controllers, then computes and injects a coordinated slowdown that turns the deployment into a bottleneck-equivalent version of a hypothetically optimized application.

summary: Figure 4 gives the architecture of Slowpoke, a system that predicts the throughput impact of hypothetically optimizing one microservice without implementing the optimization. The data plane (top) shows three Kubernetes pods, each running a Service (the middle one is the Target Service) behind Slowpoke's instrumented, API-compatible HTTP/gRPC library, alongside a lightweight POKER controller. Instrumented libraries record request counts and downstream calls, relay them to POKER over a UNIX pipe, and notify POKER when the target service crosses a request threshold. Below a dashed divider, the control plane aggregates this information during a pre-profiling phase (orange) to build a performance model, then during a slowdown phase (green) computes and coordinates POSIX-signal-based slowdowns of non-target services, producing a bottleneck-equivalent execution used to predict end-to-end throughput.
summary_zh: 图4展示Slowpoke架构：数据平面中每个Pod内的服务通过插桩HTTP/gRPC库与同置的POKER交互；控制平面先预分析负载和邻居信息，再计算并协调对非目标服务的减速，从而预测端到端吞吐量。
